chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaṭṭāb, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Khaṭṭāb, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Manī’, from Yūnus ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from his father, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: O Sadīr! Do you perform the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) every day? I said: May I be sacrificed for you, no. He said: How negligent you people are! Do you perform his Ziyārah every month? I said: No. He said: Do you perform it every year? I said: Sometimes. He said: O Sadīr! How negligent you people are toward al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) in that! Do you not know that Allah has a million angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep and perform Ziyārah and do not cease? And what is difficult for you, O Sadīr, to perform the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) five times every Friday? And he mentioned like the first hadith.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward and recommended frequency for visiting the grave of Imam al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) gently corrects Sadīr’s perceived negligence by highlighting the ceaseless worship of a million angels at the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), thereby elevating the spiritual status of human Ziyārah. This narration underscores the concept of *Ziyārah* as a continuous act of devotion rather than a sporadic ritual, reinforcing its equivalence to Hajj and ‘Umrah in reward. The emphasis on frequent visitation reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Imams' graves as spiritual hubs connecting the earthly realm with the divine presence.
